165400.overview:
IFR is a flight simulator of Cessna 172RG Cutlass light aircraft. Due to limitations of early 1980s computers it doesn't offer external cockpit view, only an instrument panel (hence the name: Instrument Flight Rules) with full set of gauges: altimeter, tachometer, artificial horizon, airspeed, turn, and rate of climb indicators. The plane is also equipped with flaps, retractable landing gear, LORAN-C inertial navigation system, ILS and ADF (picking up 4 beacons and 2 airfields on the map).

The objective is to safely navigate between 4 airfields located on the map, while avoiding terrain obstacles etc. and within the aircraft fuel limit (~30 min.); the game flight model also includes stalls, wind and turbulence (difficulty level is adjustable).

165712.overview:
A business simulator which puts you in control of a Silicon Valley software firm: you've invested $100,000 in cash in the business, and now you get to call the shots. Your goal is to expand your share of the computer software market while striving against a competing company (run by the computer or by another human player).

Each turn represents a fiscal quarter, and both companies set up a business strategy. This is done by walking your character between the company's various buildings: at R&D, development budget is assigned for up to five potential products (games, judging by their titles). Stock levels are set at Manufacturing, and retail prices are adjusted in the Sales office. Then there's Advertising, which will (literally) reach out its hand for budget.

These factors, along with your opponent's tactics, will determine your market performance - when the next quarter rolls in, you receive a financial report, and can redivide the pie accordingly. To win, you will have to balance supply and demand, read the market correctly and counter the competition's strategy. The length of the game (in quarters) is adjustable, and there's also a Monopoly mode, where both sides can try to corner the market by setting prices at below cost.

166555.overview:
The insect creatures from Terron are raining multitudes of varying bombs and bugs onto the humanoids on the planet's surface. The bugs are trying to feed on the humanoids. It is your job to stop them.

Developed by Romik Software in 1983. Distributed in North America by Laing Marketing.

168227.overview:
Island of Secrets is a typical early text adventure. The player, as a character named Alphan, must find a number of special objects of power and bring them to the starting location. This is required to restore warmth and life to the Earth. Twists to the standard formula is that the game comes with a turn limit which puts pressure on the player and his or her decisions of where to go. The player also has a strength and wisdom value. They both go down with each turn. Strength requires consumption of food to restore and wisdom can only be restored by solving puzzles. The game uses a text parser that the player uses to input commands to explore the island.

The game supports saving and loading.

218720.overview:
Interlox is a computer board game based upon Noughts & Crosses/Tic-Tac-Toe.

Played on four interlocking squares simultaneously, the goal is to place pieces on a board to align 3-in-a-row either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally, while preventing the opponent from doing the same. Pieces are placed by pressing the button corresponding to the board position. In a 2-player game, the player with the most runs of 3 after all positions are filled is the winner. Versus the computer, the goal is to prevent them from getting a run of 3 while trying to maximize player runs of 3.

419089.overview: Invaders is a side view single screen shooter inspired by the arcade game Space Invaders where you control a laser platform at the bottom of the screen, moving left or right, blasting aliens in formation above. The aliens move across the screen and when they reach the other side then they move down one place before moving across the screen in the opposite direction. As you blast the aliens, they will drop bombs and these must be avoided, or you lose one of three lives when hit. Between you and the aliens are four shields, but these take damage when hit from you or the aliens and will eventually disappear. Occasionally a Mothership moves across the top of the screen and when destroyed gives you bonus points. Two players can play, and each player takes it in turns when the other player loses a life. You can also select a skill level (1-5) before playing.

419091.overview:
Invasion is a 1-player arcade game for the VIC-20.

The player is under attack by alien vessels, which approach one at a time from the left, attempt to grab a power supply from the right of the screen, and then escape. The player must defend themselves by launching missiles from the top and bottom of the screen, one at a time, to try to destroy the alien vessel. The player receives 10 points for each vessel destroyed, and it's game over when all 4 power supplies are lost. The player receives a final rank for their defensive performance.

423573.overview:
It's a Living is a 1-player arcade game for the VIC-20.

The player has taken a job working on the production line unloading boxes at an atomic bomb company. The player is positioned in the center of the screen while 4 conveyor belts move boxes towards the player. The player can move their character's hands in 4 directions to pick up boxes as they come. Boxes approach faster as the game progresses, but so does the player's payment per box. If a box falls off the end of the conveyor belt, an atomic explosion ensues, and the employee's contract is terminated.
